cards.explanation: The answer is water, friends. Ezekiel, the prophet, sees it flowing from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (Ezekiel 47:1). It comes from under the temple itself. I think he stopped and stared, and I would have stopped right along with him.

The answer is False. At the outer gate facing east, Ezekiel sees the water trickling out from the south side (Ezekiel 47:2). It's small out there. I'd have walked right past it with my mustache full of cookie boxes, and that's exactly why you keep watching.

The answer is ankle-deep, friends. The man measures off a thousand cubits and leads Ezekiel through ankle-deep water (Ezekiel 47:3). That's the shallowest stretch of the whole walk. Barely enough to wet your toes, and the water only gets deeper from here.

The answer is waist, friends. The man measures another thousand cubits and Ezekiel is in knee-deep water. Then he measures again and leads him through waist-deep water (Ezekiel 47:4). Ankle, knee, waist, and every thousand cubits the water gets deeper.

The answer is True. After one more thousand cubits, the text says it was a river Ezekiel could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough for swimming. It was "…a river that could not be crossed on foot." (Ezekiel 47:5) Remember where it started, friends: a trickle at the temple.

The answer is a great number of trees. When Ezekiel arrives back at the bank, he sees a great number of trees along both banks of the river (Ezekiel 47:7). Trees on both sides, friends. That's a lot of shade for one river.

The answer is that it becomes fresh, friends. The man says the river flows into the Arabah, and when it empties into the Dead Sea, the water there becomes fresh (Ezekiel 47:8). The Dead Sea is the last place you'd expect a change like that. Yet the river just keeps going and gets the job done.
The answer is True. The man says, "…wherever the river flows, everything will flourish." (Ezekiel 47:9) Wherever it flows, friends. That's a river with a big job, and it does it everywhere it goes.

The answer is fish of many kinds, friends. The man says fishermen will spread their nets from En-gedi to En-eglaim to catch fish of many kinds, "…like the fish of the Great Sea." (Ezekiel 47:10) Many kinds of fish, friends. I'm picturing a very full net and a very happy fisherman.

The answer is salt. The man says the swamps and marshes will not become fresh, and "they will be left for salt." (Ezekiel 47:11) Even with everything else flourishing where the river flows, that's what he says about those spots. Salt, friends.
The answer is False. The man says, "Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail." (Ezekiel 47:12) No withering for the leaves, friends. And the fruit will not fail either.

The answer is that the water from the sanctuary flows to them, friends. That's the reason the man gives. Each month the trees will bear fruit, "…because the water from the sanctuary flows to them." (Ezekiel 47:12) The water starts at the temple and flows out to them. That's where the fruit comes from.

The answer is healing, friends. The man says, "Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing." (Ezekiel 47:12) Food from the fruit, healing from the leaves. Those trees are giving on both ends.
